A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FiSAO work. Main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A.1-A.6 are readable and matchable despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, reward analyses, and case studies in Section 4 and Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark tables, ablations, and appendix analyses, with several revised scores.

M1.justification: The entity-selection procedure, reward boundaries and normalization, token-level rewards, clipped-PPO objective, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged, including implementation explanations in Appendix A.1.

E1.justification: Training data and evaluated tasks remain unchanged. Although Table 2 drops its MMB column, MMBench results remain in Tables 3-5; the benchmark itself has not disappeared from the evaluation.

E2.justification: Removing Table 2's MMB column eliminates the reported MMBench comparisons against Vlfeedback, Human-Prefer, and POVID on both backbones. These methods remain comparators on the other benchmarks, and the open-source model comparison in Table 3 retains its membership.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1 retain the same backbones, first 8,000 training examples, training budgets, evaluation procedures, and 500-image CHAIR sample. No protocol revision accompanies the changed scores. The added lower-is-better caption clarifies existing CHAIR metrics.

E4.justification: The reward/PPO ablation, margin sensitivity study, reward-distribution and correlation analyses, and case studies are retained unchanged in Tables 4-5, Figures 1-2 and 4-10, and Appendix A.2.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-score benchmark tables and the same distribution and Pearson-correlation analyses. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, or benchmark uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes InstructBLIP+FiSAO scores: MME-P 1398.0 to 1305.3, MME-C 318.9 to 308.9, SEED 38.9 to 40.0, SQA 46.3 to 45.4, and POPE 84.7 to 83.7. LLaVA+FiSAO MM-Vet changes from 30.7 to 30.5 in Tables 2-3, while Tables 4-5 retain 30.7. Table 2 also removes its MMB results. Other results, including the appendix results, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The generative-model assumptions, Theorem 3.1, MDP formulation, and Appendix A.3.1 proof remain unchanged. The proof's different page breaks do not introduce mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about self-alignment without additional data, token-level verifier rewards, novelty, and empirical and theoretical effectiveness.

C2.justification: The interpretations of reward separation, alignment improvements, margin sensitivity, and case studies are unchanged. Appendix A.5 retains the same limitation concerning vision-encoder biases and inaccuracies. No new interpretation explains the revised scores.

D1.justification: The code-access pointer changes from an anonymous 4open.science repository in v2's reproducibility statement to a named GitHub repository in v4's abstract. Entity construction, hyperparameters, hardware, and training times remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds citations to OAG-BERT, Sheng et al. on recommendation, and Ali-Agent, while removing the MJ-Bench citation and reference. Recommendation and agent-based evaluation become additional application examples; FiSAO's central positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative and section sequence are largely preserved. v4 adds a publication header and acknowledgements, makes limited related-work and access-information edits, and introduces an unresolved 'Table ??' reference in Section 4.2 and empty parentheses in Section 2.

P2.justification: Table 2 removes the MMB column, revises bold highlighting, adds second-best underlining, and clarifies CHAIR score direction. Appendix tables and figures are repacked across pages, but the figures themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves Table 2's ranking annotations and supplies a named code pointer, but removes the preference-method MMBench comparisons and introduces an unexplained numerical inconsistency: Tables 2-3 report LLaVA+FiSAO MM-Vet as 30.5 while Tables 4-5 retain 30.7, previously consistent throughout v2. Together with the broken Section 4.2 table reference, these changes modestly weaken reporting completeness and coherence, outweighing the limited presentation improvements.
